chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of his companions from Aban from 'Ajlan Abu Salih who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) dictated to me: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful! This is what so-and-so son of so-andso gave in charity for the sake of Allah, while he was alive and sound, with his house which is in the clan of so-and-so, by its boundaries, as a charity. It shall neither be sold, nor gifted, nor inherited until the Inheritor of the heavens and the earth inherits it, and indeed he has settled in this charity so-and-so and his offspring. So when they become extinct, it is for the one in need among the Muslims.'
Humayd ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn 'Udeys from Aban from 'Abd al-Rahman from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What are the legal conditions and restrictions for a valid Islamic endowment (waqf) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (AS), establishes the foundational legal framework for *waqf* (endowment) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the donor's capacity and the perpetual nature of the asset. It introduces the concept of *waqf 'ala al-ahl* (endowment for family) transitioning to *waqf 'ala al-khalq* (endowment for the public), ensuring the property remains inalienable until the Hereafter. This ruling underscores the Shia view of waqf as a continuous charity (*sadaqah jariyah*) that preserves wealth for charitable purposes across generations.
